reason: The text attributes the Hebrew people's suffering exclusively to Egyptian oppression (נֹגְשָׂיו - 'their oppressors'), never to leadership failure. God's response frames the affliction as an external injustice requiring divine intervention: 'I have surely seen the affliction of My people... and I have heard their cry because of their oppressors.' The Hebrew leaders (elders, Moses, Aaron) are subsequently positioned as instruments of God's liberation rather than sources of the people's misery. The text contains no criticism or blame directed toward Hebrew leadership for the people's state.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
